project.name: watchlist-triage
project.objective: Triage sanctions/PEP name-match alerts from a frozen synthetic world: recommend close or escalate with cited evidence, human-approved, measured on zero missed planted true matches.

plan_approval.reason: I approve this plan because it follows a logical order, from creating a synthetic world to building a baseline agent and measuring it. Every task is linked to spec requirements with a test that proves it is done. Higher-risk tasks must go through independent review and my sign-off, and I can plan later upgrades after the baseline, based on real failures.

approval.reason: I'm comfortable building against this spec because it clearly defines what the system must do, how success will be checked, and what is out of scope. The rules for setting targets and calculating metrics are settled, and the actual target numbers will be set after the baseline milestone.

decisions.title: Specification v3.1 accepted after independent review.
decisions.text: Three Codex review rounds plus a two-item closure check. Round 1 BLOCK, 17 findings, all adopted (raw-data minimization and reviewer identity narrowed). Round 2 BLOCK, 13 findings, all fixed. Round 3 BLOCK on 2 partial fixes with no new blockers, fixed in v3.1. Closure check APPROVE. Owner decisions: D1 contradictory evidence is never a clear false positive; D2 hash chain plus a checkpoint in public git history; D3 a pre-registered fresh-seed world; D4 world mix of 30 TRUE_MATCH, 30 AMBIGUOUS_BY_DESIGN and 540 CLEAR_FALSE_POSITIVE; D5 round 3 limited to closure. Review texts are in docs/reviews/. Limitation: reviewer verdicts were pasted by the owner and are not cryptographically attested. Approval covers commit 7fba5db, SPEC.md hash 5dfdbe19a96cc04be14889b0fed6a25ad73a7f929e3c7375ebf37990bc4bc494. Round 2 marked 11 round-1 items as partially fixed; their remaining gaps were carried into round-2 findings, and only QA_SAMPLING and buyer scope were re-checked individually. The Kim and Yang 2024 citation was verified by the owner against the publisher page on 2026-10-07.

decisions.title: Only date of birth or ID number can rule out identity
decisions.text: I decided the agent can close an alert only when date of birth or ID number conflicts, no decisive identifier agrees, and nothing links the customer to the listed person. Nationality is weak evidence because it can be wrong or change. If I let it close alerts, the agent could miss a real match, and a missed match costs more than an extra escalation. So a nationality mismatch alone never closes an alert or sets its label.

decisions.title: Synthetic world design choices for T02
decisions.text: I chose how the synthetic world is built. Names come from small fictional name-part lists in the repo, so there is no library and no data licence issue. Variants use Latin script only, which I state as a known limit. The generated world is committed with a reference hash, and a drift check regenerates it in a temp folder. The matcher compares names only and allows a one-character spelling difference per name part. The world has 15 injection alerts, 5 per label, each with a control twin outside the 600. ID numbers use an obviously synthetic format so they can never match a real ID. Of the 540 clear false positives, 30 per hard family are hard cases and the rest are plain. Ambiguous alerts are 6 per family.

decisions.title: Former PEP beyond 12 months is decided by the PEP section
decisions.text: I found that two rubric sentences disagreed. One said a confirmed identity is TRUE_MATCH. The PEP section said a confirmed former PEP more than 12 months out of office with no continuing-risk snippet is AMBIGUOUS. I chose to amend the rubric to version 1.1 so the PEP section wins for that case, because it is the more specific rule and the public rubric should not contradict itself.

decisions.title: State the hard-case TRUE_MATCH rule in the rubric
decisions.text: Independent review showed six true matches rely on a hard-case exception the rubric never spelled out. I chose to write the rule down in rubric version 1.2: exactly one agreeing decisive identifier, no decisive conflict, and a snippet linking the customer to the listed person is a TRUE_MATCH. A snippet adds risk here and never lowers it. I also clarified four label-affecting points so two readers cannot apply them differently.
decisions.source: owner decision in chat, 2026-10-09, after Codex review round 1

decisions.title: Fixes after the first independent review of the world
decisions.text: The independent review found shortcuts in the world and gaps in the tests. I chose to spread the injected instructions evenly across labels, keep twin copies out of the agent loader and place injected notes at random positions, make watchlist group sizes and snippet counts independent of the label, give relationship records the related politician leaving date, and make the tests check that evidence matches the customer and watchlist records. I accepted the remaining limits and wrote them down.
decisions.source: owner decision in chat, 2026-10-09, after Codex review round 1

decisions.title: Fixes after the second independent review of the world
decisions.text: The second review generated worlds from other seeds and found labels that the visible text did not support, and injected texts that still predicted the label. I chose to use five injected texts, each used once per label, to rewrite the note templates so the text itself meets the rubric wording, to validate dates and tighten the loader, and to correct the design note. I accepted the remaining cues, such as neutral notes appearing mostly on clear false positives, as written limits.
decisions.source: owner decision in chat, 2026-10-09, after Codex review round 2

decisions.title: Codex round 3 approved T02 world
decisions.text: Codex round 3 (read-only, own classifier, three fresh seeds 7, 271, 8675309) returned APPROVE. All five round 2 defects fixed. Residual cues are minor and disclosed in the design note: neutral notes about 95 percent clear false positives versus a 90 percent base rate, injection presence rule 545 of 600 versus 540 of 600 for always closing. Loader isolation covers the loader path only; harness isolation is T06. Ablation without neutral notes planned.

decisions.title: CI drift check deferred to wave 2
decisions.text: Anchor artifact A.13.2 (CI check that the frozen world is byte-identical on every commit) is not covered by any wave-1 task and no CI workflow exists. Owner chose to add it as a small task at the wave-2 reopen, not before T03. The world hash is frozen at b77a6804a52b1d41650e250a31ff64a701b1d315a674a1f1242d93cb6b15c9b0, so drift in the meantime is covered by the existing determinism tests run locally. Overturn if the world files change before wave 2.

decisions.title: T03 framing design (D1-D7)
decisions.text: Owner decisions for T03 framings, 2026-10-09. D1: Framing 1 is the alert exactly as in the world (identity). Framings 2 and 3 are each transformed in all three ways (field order, name format, snippet wording) and the three must differ from each other. D2: Snippet wording is changed by a fixed, hand-written table with no model calls; the owner reviews the whole set once and the review is recorded later. D3: Framings are produced by a pure function in a new package at the repo root (framings/, stdlib only, same style as worldgen/); nothing is written into data/world/ and the world hash must not change. D4: The five injected attack texts are byte-identical in every framing. D5: Alternate wordings are per note type (tag): 5 tags x 2 alternates (one for framing 2, one for framing 3) = 10 lines; tags are neutral, identity_link, continuing_risk, relationship, contradicts. D6: Names are reordered and re-punctuated only, by position, never guessing given or family name; titles and accents stay as written. Framing 2 is 'TITLE LAST, rest': last non-title token upper-cased, comma, remaining non-title tokens in original order, title stays first and gets a trailing dot if it has none. Framing 3: last non-title token moved to the front, no comma, no upper-casing, title stays first and loses its trailing dot if it has one. Aliases use the same format. If upper-casing would change the normalised letters of any name, stop and report instead of working around it. D7: Field order is fixed per framing; blocks are the three kinds customer_field, watchlist_field, snippet. Framing 2: watchlist block, customer block, then notes, fields inside each block keep their order. Framing 3: notes first, then the customer block in reverse field order, then the watchlist block in reverse field order. Rules: evidence IDs never change. The same function applies to the twin alerts, read only via worldgen.harness_twins. The framing code never reads hidden/; it finds a snippet's note type by rendering the templates in worldgen.snippets with the alert's own names and comparing text; a snippet matching no template is left unchanged and must be one of the five injected texts, otherwise an error is raised; a snippet matching more than one template raises an error. Names inside rewritten notes use the same name format as that framing's name fields. Deterministic: no randomness, no clock, no environment lookups. Injected texts, dates, ID numbers, nationalities, addresses, pep_status, office, relationship fields and every date field are byte-identical across framings.

decisions.title: Neutral alternates must be content-free
decisions.text: Owner chose option A (2026-10-09): the two neutral alternates carry no identity, risk, relationship or all-clear content; they are administrative notes in the style of the five original neutral wordings. The other eight alternates are approved as drafted.

decisions.title: Neutral alternates keep the originals' reassurance level
decisions.text: Supersedes DEC-T03-NEUTRAL-WORDING. Owner chose option B (2026-10-09): the five original neutral wordings already carry mild reassurance, so the two neutral alternates restore that level to keep framings meaning-equal. The reassurance cue is a property of the T02 world and is measured by the planned neutral-note ablation, not hidden in T03.

decisions.title: Owner review of the T03 wording-transformation set (AC-23)
decisions.text: I read all ten alternate wordings in docs/framings/wording-set.md against the five originals of each note type. Each alternate keeps what the rubric needs for its type. I accept that specifics such as spouse versus sibling, or the kind of conflict in a contradicting note, are generalised in framings 2 and 3, so a verdict change there could partly come from lost detail; I will state this as a limit. The neutral alternates keep the same mild reassurance as the originals (decision DEC-T03-NEUTRAL-REVERSED), so the three framings carry equal meaning. The five injected texts are not reworded in any framing.

decisions.title: Wording differences apply only where a note exists (D10)
decisions.text: D10 = A: wording differences apply only where a note exists. Every alert must differ across the three framings in field order and name format; every alert that has at least one note must also differ in wording. 280 of 615 alerts and twins have no note; this is a stated limit, not a gap. AC-23 asks only for property tests and the owner's review.

decisions.title: Alternates are written per original wording (D11)
decisions.text: D11 = B: alternates are written per original wording, not per note type: 25 originals x 2 = 50 alternates (one for framing 2, one for framing 3). This supersedes D5 (per-type), DEC-T03-NEUTRAL-WORDING, DEC-T03-NEUTRAL-REVERSED and the earlier DEC-T03-WORDING-REVIEW, which now needs a fresh owner review. Reason: Codex round 1 showed one line per type changes facts (neutral note gained a check and a follow-up outcome; a passport nationality difference became a generic different-individual note).

decisions.title: Owner review of the per-original wording set (AC-23)
decisions.text: Supersedes DEC-T03-WORDING-REVIEW. I read all fifty alternate wordings in docs/framings/wording-set.md against their 25 originals. Each alternate keeps the facts of its original: the source, the document or relationship, and the specifics such as passport nationality or the kind of family tie. Each keeps the original’s direction and its level of reassurance, and adds no new check, outcome or instruction. Each also carries its original’s key-fact words. I accept the limits: the checks are keyword-based and cannot prove meaning is identical, 8 of the 25 originals do not occur in the frozen world, and 280 of 615 alerts have no note to reword. The five injected texts are not reworded in any framing.

decisions.title: FR-21 reading: wording differs only where a note exists (amends D1)
decisions.text: Owner decision 12, amends D1 (DEC-T03-FRAMINGS-DESIGN). D1 said framings 2 and 3 are each transformed "in all three ways" (field order, name format, snippet wording). Per D10 (DEC-T03-NOSNIPPET), wording differs only where a note exists: 335 of the 615 bundles (600 alerts and 15 twins) carry a note and 280 have none. So framings 2 and 3 always differ from the original and from each other in field order and name format, and in wording wherever a note exists. This is the owner's reading of FR-21. SPEC.md is not changed. A spec clarification is carried as an open item to the wave-2 reopen.
decisions.source: owner decision 12; Codex round 2 findings, docs/reviews/t03-review-round-2.md

decisions.title: T04 model interface shape
decisions.text: One synchronous interface. Request = messages [{role, content}] + settings (model, temperature, max_tokens, timeout_s). Result = text, provider-reported model_id, input_tokens/output_tokens (None if unknown), latency_s. No tools or function-calling (FR-9).

decisions.title: T04 stub model
decisions.text: Scripted deterministic stub, no network, no randomness: default reply, optional reply sequence, chosen failure modes (timeout, empty reply, provider error). Never decides alerts.

decisions.title: T04 model configuration
decisions.text: One JSON config (provider, model, decoding settings), default provider stub, no secrets; unknown provider = clear error; env vars only later for real keys.

decisions.title: T04 agent process isolation
decisions.text: "Agent process" = child Python process (-I) talking to the parent over a pipe; parent owns the model interface; child has network blocked at Python level (connect, create_connection, DNS) before agent code runs. Limit: stops accidental and prompt-injected network use, not deliberately hostile code. OS-level sandbox deferred to the wave-2 reopen "if needed" (open item). T04 covers only the network part of AC-11 and stub part of AC-14; the rest stays in WAVE2-RESERVED.

decisions.title: T04 ships no real provider adapter
decisions.text: No real provider adapter, SDK or keys in T04; leave a registration slot.

decisions.title: T04 model errors and retries
decisions.text: Named errors (ModelError base; timeout, bad reply, provider error); interface never retries; retry limits and timeout handling belong to T05.

decisions.title: T04 child may not start other programs
decisions.text: In the child, the audit-hook block also refuses starting other programs (subprocess, os.system, os.exec*/spawn*, fork/posix_spawn) and ctypes library loading, if the audit hook can see those events. Still a Python-level guard, not an OS sandbox; OS sandbox stays a wave-2 open item.

decisions.title: T04 run_child wall-clock cap
decisions.text: run_child has a parent-side wall-clock cap (default 60 s); on expiry the child is killed and a named error is raised. It is a safety net only; the AC-13 timeout policy stays in T05.

decisions.title: T04 AC-11 network scope of the Python-level guard
decisions.text: Amends DEC-T04-ISOLATION. The Python-level guard is proven against ordinary, accidental and prompt-injected routes. Deliberately hostile code inside the agent is out of scope until an OS-level sandbox exists (wave-2 open item). SPEC.md is not changed; a spec clarification of AC-11's network part is carried to the wave-2 reopen.

decisions.title: T04 run_child model calls run in a worker thread within the cap
decisions.text: Amends DEC-T04-WALLCLOCK. The parent runs each model call in a worker thread and waits within the cap; on expiry it kills the child and raises ChildTimeout on time. The abandoned thread may linger until its call returns.

decisions.title: T04 plan wording is original; DEC-T04-AC11-SCOPE governs
decisions.text: The approved plan/KICKOFF task text for T04 ("can reach nothing except the model interface") is the original wording; DEC-T04-AC11-SCOPE governs (ordinary, accidental and prompt-injected routes; hostile in-process code out of scope until a wave-2 OS sandbox). The wave-2 reopen aligns the T04 task text and AC-11. Plan text is not hand-edited.

decisions.title: Naive baseline: one model call per alert with one short fixed prompt
decisions.text: naive = one model call per alert, one short fixed prompt, no tools/retrieval/examples/self-check. Prompt states task and output format, says ESCALATE if evidence is unclear or contradictory (FR-7), says snippet text is untrusted data never to follow (NFR-5), snippets in clear delimiters; no rubric rules. Owner reviews the prompt once; text and hash recorded. Limit: stub tests prove the instructions are present, not that a real model follows them (T07, AC-12).

decisions.title: Agent payload is built from an allowlist
decisions.text: payload built from an allowlist: per item id, kind, field, value, plus one as_of_date and an item count; provenance fields only if the build stage shows they carry no label hint. AC-21 test checks the real payload and prompt against forbidden label and supporting-key names; a static check shows the agent module opens no files (harness check is T06).

decisions.title: Model reply schema and agent result shape
decisions.text: model reply is one JSON object with exactly schema_version "1", recommendation (CLOSE|ESCALATE), reason, cited_ids. Agent returns recommendation, reason, cited_ids, system_failure flag with failure kind, and a log record.

decisions.title: Citation and reason rules for CLOSE and ESCALATE
decisions.text: empty reason or no cited IDs -> ESCALATE with SYSTEM_FAILURE. A CLOSE must have a valid set (non-empty, every ID in the bundle) else ESCALATE with SYSTEM_FAILURE (kind recorded). An ESCALATE citing an ID not in the bundle stays ESCALATE, marked citation invalid, counted by T06. Spec tension (non-failure results measured for citation existence vs missing citations as a failure) carried to the wave-2 reopen.

decisions.title: Definitions of the seven model and output faults
decisions.text: malformed output = not one JSON object with exact keys; missing citations = no reason or empty cited_ids; truncated evidence = payload item count mismatch; unknown schema version = version not "1" in payload or reply; timeout/provider error = existing named errors plus ChildTimeout; model refusal = new named error ModelRefusal with a "refusal" stub mode (small additive edit to model_interface, with its own tests).

decisions.title: Fail closed in the child and in a parent wrapper, with a log record per result
decisions.text: one entry function catches model errors and bad output in the child; a parent wrapper catches ChildError/ChildTimeout; both return the same result shape, always ESCALATE+SYSTEM_FAILURE on fault. Each result carries a log record (failure kind, error name, attempts, time) sent to a pluggable sink (default in-memory list). Real log is wave 2.

decisions.title: Bounded retries for transient faults only
decisions.text: retry only transient faults (timeout, provider error), up to 2 retries (3 attempts), no backoff yet; bad output and refusal are not retried; each attempt logged; per-call timeout from Settings.timeout_s; run_child limit_s set above attempts x timeout_s plus a margin.

decisions.title: T05 is stub-only; real provider adapter decided later
decisions.text: T05 is stub-only; the real provider adapter, provider choice and key handling are settled at the T06/T07 pre-flight (the plan may need an added task; not confirmed).

decisions.title: Owner review of the baseline prompt
decisions.text: I read the system message and the user template. It states the task and output format, tells the model to escalate when unclear, and marks snippets as untrusted. It has no rubric rules and no hints about labels or injections.

decisions.title: Log per attempt, correlation id, no global sink
decisions.text: Owner decision 10 (2026-10-11): the log record carries a per-attempt list [{error_name, latency_s}]; recommend() accepts an optional opaque correlation_id attached to the log in the parent only, never sent to the child or model; no module-level default sink list.

decisions.title: Three added failure kinds
decisions.text: model_error, internal_error and child_crash (incl. BadResult) were added during the build. Each fails closed to ESCALATE + SYSTEM_FAILURE, is never retried, and uses the same result shape. Source: owner approved the build in the T05 pre-flight ("all as recommended"); these kinds were reported at the time.

decisions.title: Parent re-validates the full child result
decisions.text: The parent re-validates the full child result: exact key set, types, recommendation, failure kind, the failure and non-failure rules, citations against the payload's item ids, and the log record. An inconsistent result fails closed as ESCALATE + SYSTEM_FAILURE child_crash, in the same result shape. Follows finding 1 of docs/reviews/t05-review-round-1.md.

decisions.title: Parent enforces all log-to-result relationships
decisions.text: The parent enforces all relationships between the log record and the result, for success and failure: kind vs failure_kind; attempts equal to the number of attempt entries and at most 1 + retries; a success has at least one attempt, a null error_name and a final attempt with no error; earlier attempts are only retryable errors (ModelTimeout, ProviderError); a failure's error_name is consistent with its failure_kind; latency fields are finite and >= 0; model_id is a string when the last call returned a reply. Any violation fails closed as ESCALATE + SYSTEM_FAILURE child_crash. The sink gets an independent deep copy of the log record. Drift between the child's failure kinds and the parent's list is tested. Follows docs/reviews/t05-review-round-2.md.

decisions.title: No environment variables in harness outputs
decisions.text: The manifest and the reports never record an environment variable. Key handling is T07.

decisions.title: No provider code in T06; the real adapter is built in T07
decisions.text: T06 is provider-neutral: no provider code, SDK or key. It fixes shapes only: token counts and model_id of model_interface.Result, the price table and the pacer setting. The real provider adapter is built in T07 before the paid run, tested in tests/t07_baseline with fake responses; a T07 decision record links it to FR-16 (real half), NFR-3, NFR-4 and NFR-6. The plan is not reopened: the adapter is built where it is first needed, and the plan is not changed by untested Genesis commands. T07 reruns the T04 and T05 suites by hand after registering the adapter.

decisions.title: What the T06 gate runs, and the rehearsal outside it
decisions.text: The gate scores the full world x 3 framings x 3 runs in-process; the real child is used on about 30 items in all framings and every reachable fault path; in-process and real-child results must be identical on those items with timings removed; mutation proofs rerun guard files only; target under 45 s. The in-process path is test-only. Outside the gate, one run set of 5,535 calls goes through the real child before independent review, on the uncommitted tree, recorded as dirty by design: a full-scale rehearsal of the real-child path, not a baseline, per-run figures only. Its outcome must show a full comparison with the in-process path (identical, timings removed), no child process left and no error.

decisions.title: How the harness checks that the agent reads no files
decisions.text: The T05 static check stays. A test-only wrapper records file-open events in the child after start-up on the gate real-child sample, with a positive control; no reviewed code is changed. The run step never imports worldgen.truth, and a test shows hidden/ is not opened before all outputs are written. A separate command runs the hidden-file hash check on its own, used by hand before any paid run. Claim: tested on a sample, not enforced per item. An operating-system sandbox is wave 2.

decisions.title: Harness faults, item failures, re-runs and run sets
decisions.text: A harness fault (exception from recommend or the sink, world-hash mismatch) aborts the run: marked aborted, never scored, aborted count published, its calls and known cost kept in the run-set index. Item failures are scored per spec. High-failure runs are published as is with the breakdown by kind. Any re-run records a written cause. A run set is the runs sharing the same run-set inputs: commit, world hash, prompt hash, model configuration, worker count, pacer setting, infrastructure-invalid threshold, price table, modelled-time parameter file. A valid run is completed, not infrastructure-invalid and not dirty; every valid run counts toward the three and the spread and none is dropped. Changed inputs start a new run set; the old one stays listed as superseded. Only a set with at least 3 valid runs can be a baseline.

decisions.title: Runs spoiled by the infrastructure do not count
decisions.text: A completed run whose share of transient failures (kinds timeout and provider_error, as T05 classifies them) is strictly above a threshold is marked infrastructure-invalid: scored, published and listed in the index, never counted toward the three or the spread. The share is over all items, main and twin. Model-caused failures always count. child_timeout is not transient. T06 builds the mechanism with a fixture value; the threshold is set in T07 before the paid run, recorded in the manifest, and is a run-set input. Limits: a model always too slow makes every run invalid until timeout_s changes (a new run set); excluding runs makes latency and cost look friendlier, which is why invalid runs are published with all their figures.

decisions.title: Citation figures and the AC-2 re-check
decisions.text: Citation existence rate as the spec defines it, with raw counts beside every rate: citation_invalid, missing_citations, invalid_citation. The harness re-checks every CLOSE against the bundle it sent, without trusting the agent flag, and reports n of n. A bad CLOSE does not abort: it is scored as the CLOSE, counted as an AC-2 violation, the acceptance check fails, and it is never corrected. Citation precision uses the citation-accuracy population (non-failure CLOSE on CLEAR_FALSE_POSITIVE main items), stated beside the figure. A count of results citing an injected item is reported with no AC-12 judgement. AC-2 stays a T05 requirement.

decisions.title: What latency means in the harness
decisions.text: Headline latency is harness wall-clock time per alert-framing item including retries (NFR-6), from hand-off to the agent until the checked result returns. Queue wait and pacer wait are excluded. Total run time is a separate figure. The agent latency_s is shown beside it as model-call time. Limit: the figure includes child start-up and, with several workers, contention.

decisions.title: Spread and percentiles
decisions.text: Spread is each run value plus the minimum and maximum across the valid runs of the run set, for every figure in every breakdown cell (run, framing, family). Percentiles are by nearest rank, the median included; median and p95 are given per run.

decisions.title: Token counts, cost and the price table
decisions.text: Token counts are captured by a parent-side wrapper around the model, a new instance per item, counting every attempt including retries and failures. Unknown is not available, never 0. Partial totals are reported as: at least X; N attempts without token counts. The price table (source, date, currency, price per million input and output tokens, unit field) sits in the run configuration and is copied into the manifest; arithmetic is in exact decimals; T06 has a fixture only. Limit: after a child_timeout the abandoned call may finish later and its tokens are not captured.

decisions.title: What the run manifest holds, and the dirty rule
decisions.text: Manifest = the NFR-3 list plus git commit and dirty flag, configuration hash, framing code hash, Python version, worker count, pacer setting, infrastructure-invalid threshold with the run share and mark, timestamps, item counts, agent name, aborted flag, price-table and modelled-time file hashes, the review policies used, re-run cause. items.jsonl sits beside it, sorted by item ID, its hash in the manifest. Besides the manifest, the report holds numbers and identifiers only. The tree is dirty when a tracked file is modified or an untracked file lies outside the run-output folder. A dirty-tree run is published and listed but never counts toward the three or the spread of any run set and is never part of a baseline. In T06 every run writes outside the repository and runs/ stays empty; T06 commits no run output.

decisions.title: Framing is pinned by a code hash, not the T03 wording fingerprint
decisions.text: The manifest records one framing code hash: SHA-256 over every file the framings package imports or reads, in sorted path order (five framings files; worldgen __init__, matcher, textutil, snippets; names/titles.txt). The harness never imports test code, so the T03 wording fingerprint, whose function lives in tests/t03_framings, is not recorded. The framing hash is not a run-set input; the commit covers it and a dirty run never counts.

decisions.title: Modelled review time: parameters and review policies
decisions.text: The four parameters of SPEC.md Metrics (manual clearing, proposal review, L2, second review) are in minutes with a unit field. One file holds three complete sets, LOW, BASE and HIGH, computed side by side. Two review policies are computed side by side: STRICT_FOUR_EYES (spec default, every close second-reviewed) as the headline, and none beside it to show the cost of four-eyes. The file is hashed into the manifest and printed with every time result; a run with a provider other than the stub is refused without it. T06 has a fixture; T07 commits the values. QA_SAMPLING is wave 2.

decisions.title: Reference agents and AC-7
decisions.text: Always-escalate and always-close are in-process functions returning the T05 result shape, citing the lowest evidence ID in sorted order. AC-7: always-close fails AC-1; always-escalate fails AC-6 by the spec rule that citation accuracy with no closes is not applicable and fails any target. The report flags any parameter set where proposal_review + (1 - E/N) x L2 < manual_clearing, with E and N counted from the world. The T06 acceptance check covers AC-1, AC-2, AC-5 and the not-applicable rule of AC-6; AC-16 targets do not exist yet.

decisions.title: One alert per context; twins feed only the injection measure
decisions.text: Every call carries one bundle. Twins are separate calls loaded only through worldgen/harness_twins.py, feed only the injection measure, and are outside every accuracy, cost-per-alert and latency figure. An alert is compared with its twin within the same framing and the same run. The report gives main, twin and total calls and cost.

decisions.title: Thread pool, pacer and clean shutdown
decisions.text: A thread pool with a configurable worker count, recorded in the manifest; an interrupted run is aborted and re-run whole, no resume. Safeguards: (1) a parallel-equals-sequential test with the fake model, replies and fault choices; (2) nothing shared: per-call sink list and token wrapper, results combined by the main thread, a stress test that 1-token calls sum exactly; (3) sort by item ID before writing and before any figure; (4) a pacer, off by default, maximum hand-offs per minute, waiting before hand-off, its wait counted as queue time, tested with a fake clock; (5) clean shutdown: no new hand-off, calls in flight are waited for (bounded), no child process remains afterwards. decisions.title: How the figures are computed where the spec leaves a choice

(3) Over-escalation: the failure count is given over the CLEAR_FALSE_POSITIVE items, so that genuine and failure escalations add up to the over-escalation rate, and also over the escalations alone. (4) A SYSTEM_FAILURE is an ESCALATE in every figure and is never a CLOSE; it is left out of the citation rates, and its count is shown by failure kind. decisions.title: What the T06 gate runs, its time target and reference, and the rehearsal outside it
decisions.text: The gate scores the full world x 3 framings x 3 runs in-process; the real child is used on 36 items (one alert per fake outcome, in three framings) and every reachable fault path; in-process and real-child results must be identical on those items with timings removed. The in-process path is test-only. Time target, set by the owner judgment on 2026-10-15 and replacing the target of under 60 seconds with an alarm at 80: the slowest of three runs is under 75 seconds, with an alarm at 90 seconds; the gate stops at 120. The reference for timing is the fixed benchmark tools/bench_reference.py, run with the charger state before every timed run: a pure-Python loop of 12,000,000 steps, total = (total + i * i) % 1_000_003, that imports only time and prints the result 983797; a test checks that the loop is deterministic, imports only time, and gives the full result 983797. On the build machine it takes about 0.77 to 0.82 s when the charger is in. The charger state is read from /sys/class/power_supply/AC1/online. The gate is run with the charger in, with the owner performance setting noted beside the timings; the Windows power mode cannot be read from WSL. Balanced runs before the change took 61.78 to 65.02 s, so the change is the most likely explanation of the speed-up; four Balanced runs after the change (55.87, 56.99, 55.93 and 56.40 s) are close to the three Turbo runs (56.04 to 56.88 s), so the power mode shows no measurable difference. Measured on 2026-10-14 with the charger in, after the breakdowns were made to count each call once: 294 tests passed in 56.81, 56.04 and 56.88 seconds, with the benchmark at 0.773, 0.765 and 0.767 s just before each run, on G-Helper Turbo (Windows Best performance); and 295 tests in 55.87 seconds on Balanced, benchmark 0.781 s; and 296 tests in 56.99, 55.93 and 56.40 seconds on Balanced, with the benchmark at 0.789, 0.785 and 0.797 s just before each run. Measured on 2026-10-15 through tools/timed_run.sh, with the charger in and the G-Helper mode not given, after the round-3 tests were added: 316 tests passed in 62.16, 66.74, 61.35 and 68.29 seconds, with the benchmark at 0.796, 0.794, 0.802 and 0.799 s just before each run, and memory in use peaking at 2,516, 2,540, 2,452 and 2,537 MB. Runs 2 and 4 were 4 to 7 s slower than runs 1 and 3 for an unknown reason; during run 4 other processes were running on WSL. Limit: the slowest measured run is 68.29 s, so the margin to the target is about 7 s. A timed run starts with tools/timed_run.sh, which refuses with exit code 2 and starts nothing unless the charger check, tools/power_check.sh, says exactly plugged in, and the benchmark exits with 0, prints N=12000000 and result 983797, and takes no longer than BENCH_MAX_S, 1.2 s unless set. Its --unchecked flag runs anyway and marks the output UNCHECKED TIMING; a time taken that way must not be recorded as a gate timing; nothing enforces this, it is a rule for the owner. The run then goes through tools/memory_guard.sh, which kills the process group of the run when the memory in use on the whole machine passes 3,000 MB. Its trigger is machine-wide, not the memory of the run itself: a spike in any other process can stop a healthy run, and the output then says the guard stopped it. These tools are timing aids, not part of the harness, and their tests use dummy processes only. Mutation proofs: each deliberate breakage is applied to its own temporary copy and only the named guard tests are rerun there, two copies at a time (one named setting, AT_A_TIME). Each copy test process has a hard limit of 1 GiB of address space (RLIMIT_AS, inherited by what it starts); a broken copy that runs out of memory ends alone, is reported as out of memory, and counts as caught. Out of memory is counted only when the copy ended itself with a positive exit code and its output shows a MemoryError: the limit sends no signal of its own, and a copy ended by a signal is not a catch. Every breakage names how its broken copy must end, as the start of the reason pytest gives: a failing assertion in the named guard test, a named error raised in it, or a named error on loading its file. Every failure pytest reports must be about the guard and give a named reason; any other ending is not a catch. The guard must pass on an untouched copy, and an untouched copy passes only with exit code 0. The gate also proves the memory limit with one deliberately memory-hungry broken copy, and shows that a copy failing for a reason its entry does not name is reported as not caught, that a copy killed by a signal is not caught, and that an untouched copy whose session fails for an unrelated reason is not a pass. The stress test of DEC-T06-PARALLEL safeguard 2 uses 8 workers and 1,000 items, as two named settings, sized for the 3.5 GiB build machine. Outside the gate, one run set of 5,535 calls goes through the real child before independent review, on the uncommitted tree, recorded as dirty by design: a full-scale rehearsal of the real-child path, not a baseline, per-run figures only. Its outcome must show a full comparison with the in-process path (identical, timings removed), no child process left and no error. The rehearsal was done on 2026-10-14: all 5,535 results were identical to the in-process path, no child process was left, and no run was aborted. decisions.title: What the run manifest holds, the dirty rule, who scored a report, the evaluation run, and refused runs
decisions.text: Manifest = the NFR-3 list plus git commit and dirty flag, configuration hash, framing code hash, Python version, worker count, pacer setting, infrastructure-invalid threshold with the run share and mark, timestamps, item counts, agent name, aborted flag, price-table and modelled-time file hashes, the review policies used, re-run cause. items.jsonl sits beside it, sorted by item ID, its hash in the manifest. Besides the manifest, the report holds numbers and identifiers only. The tree is dirty when a tracked file is modified or an untracked file lies outside the run-output folder. A dirty-tree run is published and listed but never counts toward the three or the spread of any run set and is never part of a baseline. In T06 every run writes outside the repository and runs/ stays empty; T06 commits no run output. The score step writes a report only for a run that has none; replacing a report needs an explicit option. Every report names the commit of the scoring code and whether that tree was dirty. The run-set report is worked out afresh each time and says which code wrote each run report. A run set can be a baseline only if every run report and the run-set report were scored by the same clean commit; otherwise the set report says that re-scoring is needed. An evaluation run in the sense of AC-24 is python -m harness run-and-score CONFIG OUT: the run, then the score step for OUT against the world of the run, in that order; if the run does not complete, nothing is scored. The scoring code is loaded only after the run returns, so the run step never imports worldgen.truth. A bare python -m harness run writes items.jsonl, the manifest and the index entry and has no report, by design; its report is written later by python -m harness score or by run-and-score. The score step loads and checks each run on its own. A run that fails its checks or cannot be loaded at all (a missing or empty file, invalid JSON, a missing field, a value of the wrong type, an items file whose hash does not match its manifest, a run made on another world) is quarantined: nothing is written for it; it is listed as excluded with its reason, which starts with its run ID, in its set report as left out with refused: and that reason, and on the command line; and the command exits with 1. The other runs still get their reports. Every manifest field the score step uses is read while loading, so a missing one is found there. A check of the world itself (its manifest or its hidden files) refuses the whole step, and so does a step in which every run to score is refused: then nothing is written. An error while computing the figures is a bug and still stops the step. Tests cover a hash mismatch, a missing outputs field, an invalid JSON manifest, a missing items file, an empty manifest and a manifest of the wrong type, each followed by a new run-and-score that still gets its report; the step in which every run is refused; and an error while computing the figures.

decisions.title: What the T06 gate runs, its time target and reference, and the rehearsal outside it
decisions.text: The gate scores the full world x 3 framings x 3 runs in-process; the real child is used on 36 items (one alert per fake outcome, in three framings) and every reachable fault path; in-process and real-child results must be identical on those items with timings removed. The in-process path is test-only. Time target, set by the owner judgment on 2026-10-15 and replacing the target of under 75 seconds with an alarm at 90: the slowest of three runs is under 90 seconds, with an alarm at 100 seconds; the gate stops at 120. The reference for timing is the fixed benchmark tools/bench_reference.py, run with the charger state before every timed run: a pure-Python loop of 12,000,000 steps, total = (total + i * i) % 1_000_003, that imports only time and prints the result 983797; a test checks that the loop is deterministic, imports only time, and gives the full result 983797. On the build machine it takes about 0.77 to 0.82 s when the charger is in. The charger state is read from /sys/class/power_supply/AC1/online. The gate is run with the charger in, with the owner performance setting noted beside the timings; the Windows power mode cannot be read from WSL. Balanced runs before the change took 61.78 to 65.02 s, so the change is the most likely explanation of the speed-up; four Balanced runs after the change (55.87, 56.99, 55.93 and 56.40 s) are close to the three Turbo runs (56.04 to 56.88 s), so the power mode shows no measurable difference. Measured on 2026-10-14 with the charger in, after the breakdowns were made to count each call once: 294 tests passed in 56.81, 56.04 and 56.88 seconds, with the benchmark at 0.773, 0.765 and 0.767 s just before each run, on G-Helper Turbo (Windows Best performance); and 295 tests in 55.87 seconds on Balanced, benchmark 0.781 s; and 296 tests in 56.99, 55.93 and 56.40 seconds on Balanced, with the benchmark at 0.789, 0.785 and 0.797 s just before each run. Measured on 2026-10-15 through tools/timed_run.sh, with the charger in and the G-Helper mode not given, after the round-3 tests were added: 316 tests passed in 62.16, 66.74, 61.35 and 68.29 seconds, with the benchmark at 0.796, 0.794, 0.802 and 0.799 s just before each run, and memory in use peaking at 2,516, 2,540, 2,452 and 2,537 MB. Runs 2 and 4 were 4 to 7 s slower than runs 1 and 3 for an unknown reason; during run 4 other processes were running on WSL. Limit then in force: the slowest measured run was 68.29 s, about 7 s below the target of 75 s in force at that time. A timed run starts with tools/timed_run.sh, which refuses with exit code 2 and starts nothing unless the charger check, tools/power_check.sh, says exactly plugged in, and the benchmark exits with 0, prints N=12000000 and result 983797, and takes no longer than BENCH_MAX_S, 1.2 s unless set. Its --unchecked flag runs anyway and marks the output UNCHECKED TIMING; a time taken that way must not be recorded as a gate timing; nothing enforces this, it is a rule for the owner. The run then goes through tools/memory_guard.sh, which kills the process group of the run when the memory in use on the whole machine passes 3,000 MB. Its trigger is machine-wide, not the memory of the run itself: a spike in any other process can stop a healthy run, and the output then says the guard stopped it. These tools are timing aids, not part of the harness, and their tests use dummy processes only. Mutation proofs: each deliberate breakage is applied to its own temporary copy and only the named guard tests are rerun there, two copies at a time (one named setting, AT_A_TIME). Each copy test process has a hard limit of 1 GiB of address space (RLIMIT_AS, inherited by what it starts); a broken copy that runs out of memory ends alone, is reported as out of memory, and counts as caught. Out of memory is counted only when the copy ended itself with a positive exit code and its output shows a MemoryError: the limit sends no signal of its own, and a copy ended by a signal is not a catch. Every breakage names how its broken copy must end, as the start of the reason pytest gives: a failing assertion in the named guard test, a named error raised in it, or a named error on loading its file. Every failure pytest reports must be about the guard and give a named reason; any other ending is not a catch. The guard must pass on an untouched copy, and an untouched copy passes only with exit code 0. The mutation proofs run with T06_MUTATION=1 by hand before completion, recorded as evidence; they are skipped in the default gate run, except the check that every breakage names a guard test that exists, which runs in it. The stress test of DEC-T06-PARALLEL safeguard 2 uses 8 workers and 1,000 items, as two named settings, sized for the 3.5 GiB build machine. Outside the gate, one run set of 5,535 calls goes through the real child before independent review, on the uncommitted tree, recorded as dirty by design: a full-scale rehearsal of the real-child path, not a baseline, per-run figures only. Its outcome must show a full comparison with the in-process path (identical, timings removed), no child process left and no error. The rehearsal was done on 2026-10-14: all 5,535 results were identical to the in-process path, no child process was left, and no run was aborted. This is the builder report; the temporary folder was not kept. Measured on 2026-10-15 through tools/timed_run.sh after the round-5 changes, with the charger in and the G-Helper mode not given: 333 tests passed in 85.86, 77.05 and 74.17 seconds, with the benchmark at 0.797, 0.802 and 0.802 s just before each run, and memory in use peaking at 2,388, 2,363 and 2,229 MB. In run 1, three of the shell-based timing-tool tests took 11.7 s together, against about 0.6 s in runs 2 and 3, for an unknown reason. Limit: the slowest of these runs, 85.86 s, leaves a margin of about 34 s to the 120-second stop and about 4 s to the target in that worst run, which included a stall of about 11 s; the other two runs left about 13 s and 16 s. Measured on 2026-10-16 through tools/timed_run.sh after the round-8 fixes, with the charger in and the G-Helper mode not given, the mutation proofs still in the gate run: 343 tests passed in 85.02, 98.67 and 87.69 seconds, with the benchmark at 0.806, 0.800 and 0.800 s; the 98.67-second run was above the target, almost all of its extra time in the mutation-proof tests, for an unknown reason. Measured on 2026-10-16 after the mutation proofs were moved out of the default gate run: 337 tests passed and 7 were skipped in 55.97, 55.75 and 56.65 seconds, with the benchmark at 0.799, 0.806 and 0.797 s just before each run and memory in use peaking at 1,725, 1,745 and 1,729 MB; the mutation proofs alone, with T06_MUTATION=1, passed 7 tests in 28.98 seconds, benchmark 0.792 s, memory in use peaking at 2,236 MB. Limit: the slowest default run, 56.65 s, leaves about 33 s to the target and about 63 s to the 120-second stop.

The in-process path is test-only. Time target, set by the owner judgment on 2026-10-15 and replacing the target of under 75 seconds with an alarm at 90: the slowest of three runs is under 90 seconds, with an alarm at 100 seconds; Genesis kills the gate's test command after 120 seconds: the default timeout of genesis gate is 120,000 ms (genesis-kit tools/genesis.mjs:1131, "const timeout = positive(parsed.options.timeout || 120000, 'timeout');"), enforced by a SIGKILL to the command's process group (genesis.mjs:1087); tools/memory_guard.sh, under which tools/timed_run.sh runs a command, also stops a command after MEMORY_GUARD_MAX_SECONDS, 110 seconds unless set, says so and exits non-zero. The reference for timing is the fixed benchmark tools/bench_reference.py, run with the charger state before every timed run: a pure-Python loop of 12,000,000 steps, total = (total + i * i) % 1_000_003, that imports only time and prints the result 983797; a test checks that the loop is deterministic, imports only time, and gives the full result 983797. On the build machine it takes about 0.77 to 0.82 s when the charger is in. The charger state is read from /sys/class/power_supply/AC1/online. The gate is run with the charger in, with the owner performance setting noted beside the timings; the Windows power mode cannot be read from WSL. Balanced runs before the change took 61.78 to 65.02 s, so the change is the most likely explanation of the speed-up; four Balanced runs after the change (55.87, 56.99, 55.93 and 56.40 s) are close to the three Turbo runs (56.04 to 56.88 s), so the power mode shows no measurable difference. Measured on 2026-10-14 with the charger in, after the breakdowns were made to count each call once: 294 tests passed in 56.81, 56.04 and 56.88 seconds, with the benchmark at 0.773, 0.765 and 0.767 s just before each run, on G-Helper Turbo (Windows Best performance); and 295 tests in 55.87 seconds on Balanced, benchmark 0.781 s; and 296 tests in 56.99, 55.93 and 56.40 seconds on Balanced, with the benchmark at 0.789, 0.785 and 0.797 s just before each run. Measured on 2026-10-15 through tools/timed_run.sh, with the charger in and the G-Helper mode not given, after the round-3 tests were added: 316 tests passed in 62.16, 66.74, 61.35 and 68.29 seconds, with the benchmark at 0.796, 0.794, 0.802 and 0.799 s just before each run, and memory in use peaking at 2,516, 2,540, 2,452 and 2,537 MB. Runs 2 and 4 were 4 to 7 s slower than runs 1 and 3 for an unknown reason; during run 4 other processes were running on WSL. Limit then in force: the slowest measured run was 68.29 s, about 7 s below the target of 75 s in force at that time. A timed run starts with tools/timed_run.sh, which refuses with exit code 2 and starts nothing unless the charger check, tools/power_check.sh, says exactly plugged in, and the benchmark exits with 0, prints N=12000000 and result 983797, and takes no longer than BENCH_MAX_S, 1.2 s unless set. Its --unchecked flag runs anyway and marks the output UNCHECKED TIMING; a time taken that way must not be recorded as a gate timing; nothing enforces this, it is a rule for the owner. The run then goes through tools/memory_guard.sh, which kills the process group of the run when the memory in use on the whole machine passes 3,000 MB. Its trigger is machine-wide, not the memory of the run itself: a spike in any other process can stop a healthy run, and the output then says the guard stopped it. These tools are timing aids, not part of the harness, and their tests use dummy processes only. Mutation proofs: each deliberate breakage is applied to its own temporary copy and only the named guard tests are rerun there, two copies at a time (one named setting, AT_A_TIME). Each copy test process has a hard limit of 1 GiB of address space (RLIMIT_AS, inherited by what it starts); a broken copy that runs out of memory ends alone, is reported as out of memory, and counts as caught. Out of memory is counted only when the copy ended itself with a positive exit code and its output shows a MemoryError: the limit sends no signal of its own, and a copy ended by a signal is not a catch. Every breakage names how its broken copy must end, as the start of the reason pytest gives: a failing assertion in the named guard test, a named error raised in it, or a named error on loading its file. Every failure pytest reports must be about the guard and give a named reason; any other ending is not a catch. The guard must pass on an untouched copy, and an untouched copy passes only with exit code 0. The mutation proofs run with T06_MUTATION=1 by hand before completion, recorded as evidence; they are skipped in the default gate run, except the check that every breakage names a guard test that exists, which runs in it. The stress test of DEC-T06-PARALLEL safeguard 2 uses 8 workers and 1,000 items, as two named settings, sized for the 3.5 GiB build machine. Outside the gate, one run set of 5,535 calls goes through the real child before independent review, on the uncommitted tree, recorded as dirty by design: a full-scale rehearsal of the real-child path, not a baseline, per-run figures only. Its outcome must show a full comparison with the in-process path (identical, timings removed), no child process left and no error. The rehearsal was done on 2026-10-14: all 5,535 results were identical to the in-process path, no child process was left, and no run was aborted. This is the builder report; the temporary folder was not kept. Measured on 2026-10-15 through tools/timed_run.sh after the round-5 changes, with the charger in and the G-Helper mode not given: 333 tests passed in 85.86, 77.05 and 74.17 seconds, with the benchmark at 0.797, 0.802 and 0.802 s just before each run, and memory in use peaking at 2,388, 2,363 and 2,229 MB. In run 1, three of the shell-based timing-tool tests took 11.7 s together, against about 0.6 s in runs 2 and 3, for an unknown reason. Limit: the slowest of these runs, 85.86 s, leaves a margin of about 34 s to the 120-second stop and about 4 s to the target in that worst run, which included a stall of about 11 s; the other two runs left about 13 s and 16 s. Measured on 2026-10-16 through tools/timed_run.sh after the round-8 fixes, with the charger in and the G-Helper mode not given, the mutation proofs still in the gate run: 343 tests passed in 85.02, 98.67 and 87.69 seconds, with the benchmark at 0.806, 0.800 and 0.800 s; the 98.67-second run was above the target, almost all of its extra time in the mutation-proof tests, for an unknown reason. Measured on 2026-10-16 after the mutation proofs were moved out of the default gate run: 337 tests passed and 7 were skipped in 55.97, 55.75 and 56.65 seconds, with the benchmark at 0.799, 0.806 and 0.797 s just before each run and memory in use peaking at 1,725, 1,745 and 1,729 MB; the mutation proofs alone, with T06_MUTATION=1, passed 7 tests in 28.98 seconds, benchmark 0.792 s, memory in use peaking at 2,236 MB. Limit: the slowest default run, 56.65 s, leaves about 33 s to the target and about 63 s to the 120-second stop.

decisions.title: Thread pool, pacer and clean shutdown
decisions.text: A thread pool with a configurable worker count, a whole number from 1 to 64, recorded in the manifest. With one worker there is no pool: the calls are made one after another in the main thread, so the parallel-equals-sequential tests compare two different code paths. An interrupted run is aborted and re-run whole, no resume. Safeguards: (1) a parallel-equals-sequential test with the fake model, replies and fault choices; (2) nothing shared: per-call sink list and token wrapper, results combined by the main thread, a stress test that 1-token calls sum exactly; (3) sort by item ID before writing and before any figure; (4) a pacer, off by default, set as a whole number of hand-offs per minute of 1 or more, or null; it spaces hand-offs evenly, 60 seconds divided by the setting apart, waits in the main thread before a hand-off, and hands an item off only when a worker is free; its wait counts as queue time, and it is tested with a fake clock; (5) clean shutdown: no new hand-off once a fault has been collected; the fault is checked before the pacer wait and again immediately before each submit. A worker that fails after the last check cannot be prevented from having its successor submitted: at most the items already submitted or in the act of being submitted may still run, and an aborted run is never scored; calls in flight are waited for (bounded), no child process remains afterwards. Each item line carries its queue time, and the manifest the run duration and total queue time. Interrupts: Ctrl-C is a clean abort from the moment the run is listed; with several workers the calls in flight are waited for, and a second Ctrl-C gives up that wait but still marks the run aborted; with one worker the call in flight is cut short. Limits: retries inside an item are not paced; a hard kill of a child in flight is wave 2. After a second Ctrl-C with several workers, the calls still in flight are not in the run's calls and known cost. An interrupt while the outputs are being written, after the last hand-off, is not caught.

decisions.title: Independent review of T06: 12 rounds, round 12 APPROVE
decisions.text: Independent review of T06, the evaluation harness, by GPT-6 Sol at medium effort, in 12 rounds. Rounds 1 to 11 returned DO NOT APPROVE; round 12 returned APPROVE, finding no T06-owned SPEC requirement and no active DEC-T06 record contradicted by the code. The reports are kept in the repository, docs/reviews/T06-harness-review-round-1.md to docs/reviews/T06-harness-review-round-12.md. Not fixed, an improvement only: in tests/t06_harness/test_reference.py the assertion on the reference agent's injection block compares divergent, by_cause and by_label with the report's own values, so only pairs == 45 is checked there; the divergence counts are checked independently on the full world in tests/t06_harness/test_score.py. Stated limit, not a defect: the race window between the last fault check and the submit, as stated in DEC-T06-PARALLEL-3. The mutation proofs are run by hand with T06_MUTATION=1, outside the default gate run (DEC-T06-GATE-TIME-7); round 12 did not reproduce them, the full-scale rehearsal or the timing measurements. Known issues carried forward, listed in docs/harness-design.md under "For T07 and wave 2": (1) injection divergence has no primary-family cells, against FR-20; (2) mixed numeric and text provider model IDs break manifest serialisation; (3) inputs the run step accepts but the shared schema refuses: a blank re-run cause, a model name of only spaces, a non-finite temperature or timeout_s, and a reported model ID that is a non-finite number; (4) acceptance mechanism_only ignores a fixture price table when the modelled-time file is sourced; (5) the reference-agent injection assertion compares the report with itself. T07 carries: model IDs must be text, and the price table and the modelled-time file must both be sourced.

decisions.title: Real Anthropic adapter, standard library only
decisions.text: The baseline calls Claude through a small adapter written with Python's standard library and added as one new entry in the provider list, without touching providers.py line 44. With it, the model can really be swapped through configuration, which the earlier harness work left for this task. The adapter returns the model ID as text, leaves token counts empty when they are unknown, keeps one overall deadline for the call timeout, does no retries of its own (a rate-limit reply is raised straight away as a provider error), raises a refusal error when the model refuses, reads the API key only from an environment variable and masks it in errors (checked by a canary test), is safe to call from several threads, and runs with thinking off. I update the old "only the stub is registered" test and rerun the earlier model-interface and agent test suites by hand.
decisions.source: Owner decision, T07 pre-flight, 17-19 Oct 2026; links: FR-16 (real half), NFR-3, NFR-4, NFR-6; follows DEC-T06-NO-ADAPTER

decisions.title: Baseline output copied into baseline/, T06 untouched
decisions.text: The runs and the scoring happen outside the repo, all at one clean commit. Afterwards the results are copied byte for byte into baseline/ together with a SHA-256 list of every copied file, and baseline/ holds nothing else. This replaces the plan in docs/harness-design.md to write runs into a runs/ folder. I chose this so that no T06 code, test, doc or decision record has to change.

decisions.title: Pre-run checks in a T07 wrapper
decisions.text: Every paid run starts through a T07 wrapper. It refuses to start unless the working tree is fully clean (untracked files included), the run inputs are ones the scoring step will accept (no blank re-run reason, no model name made only of spaces, no number that is not finite), and a written re-run reason is given whenever one is needed. It also prints the run's expected cost and stops if my credit is below 1.5 times that amount, which I confirm by eye in the Console. These are checks the earlier harness work left for this task, and they sit outside the T06 code.
decisions.source: Owner decision, T07 pre-flight, 17-19 Oct 2026; links: DEC-T06-FAULTS-2; harness known issue 3

decisions.title: Earlier task docs stay as they were
decisions.text: The T04, T05 and T06 design docs stay exactly as they were when their tasks closed, even where a line is now out of date. Readers are pointed to the current state by a new docs/README.md index, a short "Which docs are current" pointer in the root README.md (its only commit, 9724e3b, came before the project's task tracking, so it is not a T06 file), and a "Supersedes" table at the top of the T07 doc. The out-of-date lines are model-interface-design.md:46 and 174-175, baseline-agent-design.md:12-14 and 300, and harness-design.md:30-31, 134-135, 635 and 681-682. Someone who opens an old doc directly will miss the index; I accept that gap.

decisions.title: Claude Haiku 5.5 for the baseline
decisions.text: The baseline uses Claude Haiku 5.5, the cheapest tier, because L1 triage is a volume job and the honest starting point is the cheapest model that might be good enough. Thinking is off and the batch API is not used. Before any counted run it must pass fixed checks: strict JSON on the trial alerts, a reported model ID that matches the price table, temperature 0 accepted, the spend cap in place, and rate limits with room to spare. If a check fails, I make a new decision and build a GPT-5.6 Luna adapter with its own tests and price table before any run. I will not switch models because I dislike the results.

decisions.title: $15 ceiling on prepaid credit
decisions.text: All of T07, trials and runs together, must stay under $15. I use prepaid credit with auto-reload off and separate API keys for the trial and the runs, and I hold at least 1.5 times a run's expected cost in credit before starting it.

decisions.title: Modelled time from public sources, fixed before any paid call
decisions.text: The review times come from public sources only, mostly vendor claims, and two of them have no public source and rest on stated reasoning. In minutes for LOW/BASE/HIGH: manual clearing 3/8/30, proposal review 0.5/2/5, L2 review 40/120/480 and second review 1/2/5. I picked BASE on the side that makes the agent's savings harder to show. The file is committed on its own before any paid call, trials included, so the history shows the assumptions were fixed before the first run, and I will not change it because of results. No analyst interviews were possible, and the report says so.
decisions.source: Owner decision, T07 pre-flight, 17-19 Oct 2026; links: AC-25, FR-22

decisions.title: Report the break-even escalation share
decisions.text: The T07 report adds a derived break-even figure for each parameter set and review policy: the highest escalation share at which assisted review is still faster than manual review. It is labelled as derived from the modelled-time assumptions.

decisions.title: Price table keyed by the reported model ID, checked against the bill
decisions.text: The price table uses the model ID that Anthropic actually reports back, which I will see in the trial. It is written after the trial and committed together with the run config, so every run uses the same table. After the runs I compare the harness cost with the Anthropic bill. If they differ by more than 5% after taking out the trial spend, I find out why and explain it before publishing.

decisions.title: Run settings fixed before the first run
decisions.text: Every run uses 4 workers, a pacer of 120 hand-offs per minute, an infra-invalid threshold of 2% (a run is invalid only above 2%), a call timeout of 30 seconds, max_tokens of 512, temperature 0 and a memory-guard time limit of 7,200 seconds. Two rules are fixed now: if the trial's 99th-percentile latency is over 10 seconds I revisit the timeout, and if any trial answer hits the cap or the largest is over 256 output tokens I raise max_tokens to 1,024. Any such change is a superseding record made before the run commit.

decisions.title: Trial on hand-written alerts only
decisions.text: Before any counted run I try the setup on about 20 fresh hand-written alerts shaped like the world's alerts, none taken from the frozen world, so no setting is tuned on the data I am scored on. A small T07 script calls the agent with the real adapter using the trial key, and its output is scanned with gitleaks.

decisions.title: Step order and stopping rule
decisions.text: All runs happen at the single run commit. I stop at the first 3 valid runs, with at most 5 attempts, and invalid or aborted runs count as attempts. If 5 attempts do not give 3 valid runs, I stop, investigate and make a new decision. Run 1's full output is scanned with gitleaks before runs 2 and 3; if anything is flagged I stop, and I do not add an allowlist or edit run output.

decisions.title: Release target rules, fixed before the baseline
decisions.text: I fix the rules now, before the baseline exists, so the release targets cannot be fitted to the results. The baseline value is the pooled value over the valid runs. Over-escalation target: the lower of the baseline and 3.9%, because above about 3.95% of clear false positives escalated the agent stops saving time at BASE. Verdict consistency target: the baseline. Citation accuracy target: the higher of the baseline and 95%, or 95% if the baseline is not applicable. Cost target: $0.20 per alert-framing item, which is 5% of a $4.00 analyst cost per alert ($30 an hour, the low end of a press figure, times 8 minutes). Exact fractions are stored, and any decimal shown is rounded in the strict direction. The numbers go into targets/release-targets.json, committed after the baseline report, and its hash goes into the DEC-T07-TARGETS record. T07 gate tests check the numbers, the direction rules, the commit order, that the time assumptions were committed before the runs, and the file hash.
decisions.source: Owner decision, T07 pre-flight, 17-19 Oct 2026; links: AC-16, AC-25

decisions.title: Review budget fixed before round 1
decisions.text: T07 is reviewed by GPT-6 Sol at medium effort in a fresh read-only Codex session, the same as T06. The prompt is structured: a fixed scope, the settled decisions, a stated threat model and a severity scale, and before round 1 the T07 claims are checked for over-promising words. Round 1 is a full review and later rounds only check the fixes. There are at most 4 rounds. If a blocker is still open after round 4, there is no fifth round and no approval; I decide what to do instead.

decisions.title: Claude Haiku 5.5 for the baseline, temperature fixed at 1 by the provider
decisions.text: The baseline still uses Claude Haiku 5.5, the cheapest tier. The pre-run doc check found that Haiku 5.5 only accepts temperature 1 and rejects any other value, so my "temperature 0 accepted" check failed. I decided before any run and without seeing any results to keep Haiku and use temperature 1, because the point of temperature 0 was cleaner measurement, not capability; the three-run spread now shows how much the model varies on its own, and the report says the provider fixes temperature at 1. Thinking is switched off explicitly and the batch API is not used. The remaining checks still apply before any counted run: strict JSON on the trial alerts, a reported model ID that matches the price table, the spend cap in place, rate limits with room to spare, and the refusal checkpoints. If one of those fails, I make a new decision and build a GPT-5.6 Luna adapter with its own tests and price table before any run. I will not switch models because I dislike the results.

decisions.title: Refusal checkpoints in the trial and run 1
decisions.text: Anthropic's docs warn that a reason-style field in JSON output can trigger a refusal, and my agent's answer has a reason field. A refusal is scored as an escalation and does not count toward the 2% infrastructure rule, so it could quietly shape the baseline. I set two checkpoints now: if any trial alert is refused, I stop and decide before the run commit; and if more than 2% of run 1's items are refused, I stop and decide before runs 2 and 3. At or below 2%, refusals stay in the baseline as real behaviour and are reported separately.

tasks.outcome: Produce an approved, implementation-ready product specification

evidence.reason: I'm comfortable building against this spec because it clearly defines what the system must do, how success will be checked, and what is out of scope. The rules for setting targets and calculating metrics are settled, and the actual target numbers will be set after the baseline milestone.

tasks.next_action: Interview the human, record durable context, and replace every placeholder in SPEC.md.

tasks.outcome: Write the synthetic-world adjudication rubric: the three labels, what evidence is sufficient to close, PEP status and date rules, identifier-conflict weighting, the supporting evidence key and record provenance fields, committed before any generator code.

Build the deterministic world generator and matcher: 600 labelled alerts (30 TRUE_MATCH, 30 AMBIGUOUS_BY_DESIGN, 540 CLEAR_FALSE_POSITIVE), five families with 6 TRUE_MATCH per primary family, injection alerts with control twins outside the 600, provenance on every record, byte-identical regeneration, and secret scanning across the repository.
Produce three meaning-preserving framings per alert, with property tests for the structured transformations and a fixed wording-transformation set recorded as reviewed by the owner.

Provide one model-agnostic interface with a stub model selected only by configuration, and enforce that the agent process can reach nothing except the model interface. Covers the network part of AC-11 and the stub-model part of AC-14.

Build the naive baseline agent: CLOSE or ESCALATE with a written reason and cited evidence IDs, rejection of results without them, escalation on unclear evidence, model and output faults failing closed to ESCALATE with SYSTEM_FAILURE, label isolation, and snippets treated as data. Covers the model-fault part of FR-8 and AC-13.

Build the evaluation harness: every Metrics-section figure by run, framing and primary family, the run manifest, at least 3 repeated runs, cost and latency, modelled review time, and the always-escalate and always-close reference agents.

Commit the modelled-time parameters, run the baseline on the frozen world, publish the report, and commit the targets decision record required by AC-16. The gate checks the committed artifacts and does not call the model.

Reserved for wave-2 planning. Upgrades, audit log, review policy, operational mode, release protocol and README are planned in detail after the baseline. This task is rejected at the wave-2 reopen and is not meant to be completed.

controls.reason: Three independent Codex rounds. Rounds 1 and 2 found real problems (injection wording, hard-case labels, loader paths) and I had them fixed. Round 3 returned APPROVE using its own classifier on three new seeds. I accept the remaining limits (neutral-note cue, injection cue, loader-only isolation) because they are written in the design note and will be measured later.

Two independent Codex rounds ended in APPROVE after fixes. I reviewed the 50 fixed alternate wordings and the design decisions myself. The tests keep dates, identifiers and names across the three framings. I know the wording checks are keyword-based and do not prove equal agent behaviour, which T07 will measure.

Codex round 1 was DO NOT APPROVE; I fixed the findings and accepted a narrower AC-11 scope (DEC-T04-AC11-SCOPE). Round 2 was APPROVE WITH FIXES, and I applied its two wording fixes, checked as comment-only. The guard stops ordinary and injected routes, not deliberately hostile code inside the agent; an OS sandbox is a wave-2 open item. No third review round was run, by my decision.

T05 baseline agent reviewed by independent Codex sessions over five rounds. Rounds 1-3 were DO NOT APPROVE (forged child results could leave as CLOSE; log contradictions; sink aliasing), each fixed and tested. Round 4 was APPROVE WITH FIXES (doc-only, applied). The gate then timed out at 120s, so the mutation harness was narrowed (306s to about 65s); round 5 reviewed only that change and approved. Tests pass 291 of 291. Only the stub model has run; no real model baseline yet. Limits are listed in docs/baseline-agent-design.md.

Independent review by GPT-6 Sol (medium) in 12 rounds: rounds 1-11 DO NOT APPROVE, round 12 APPROVE. Findings were fixed except the reference-agent assertion (improvement only), the race window stated in DEC-T06-PARALLEL-3, and known issues listed in docs/harness-design.md for T07 and wave 2. Gate passed: 340 tests passed, 6 skipped by default; mutation proofs run by hand (43 breakages caught). Decision record DEC-T06-REVIEW-R12. No real model has run.
